Statements that follow a `return`, `throw`, `break`, or `continue` in the same block never run. Neither does code after a loop that never ends. It is either dead code to delete, or code that was meant to run and sits in the wrong place.

Function declarations and `var` declarations without a value are hoisted, so they are not reported.

This rule is on by default in JavaScript files. It is off in TypeScript files, where TypeScript finds unreachable code itself.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
function price(item) {
  return item.price * item.quantity;
  console.log("computed", item.id);
}
```

{/* bad */}
```js
while (true) {
  poll();
}
cleanUp();
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
function price(item) {
  console.log("computing", item.id);
  return item.price * item.quantity;
}
```

{/* good */}
```js
function area(shape) {
  return width() * shape.height;

  function width() {
    return shape.width;
  }
}
```

`super()` creates the fields of a subclass. If the constructor never calls it, the fields are reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
class Admin extends User {
  role = "admin";

  constructor() {
    return loadAdmin();
  }
}
```
